adjudicatedFromGaps.note: Both gaps declared by the php wave (#268 family) were adjudicated 2026-09-29 and promoted to RULED decisions PHPD31/PHPD32. The lane now declares 0 gaps. Neither was a coverage or extraction defect: both described a deliberate language boundary (text outside <?php, and ini/shell constructs) that the old wording recorded as unfinished work.

decisions.question: PHP property access `$this->balance`, `$obj->name`, `$this->svc->inner` parses as member_access_expression — when is it a READ (uses) vs a WRITE?
decisions.resolution: A member_access_expression that is the FIRST child of an assignment_expression is a WRITE (never a use). A member_call_expression / nullsafe_member_call_expression receiver is a call target, not a read. Everything else inside a method body emits uses -> the member name (isMemberRead). Node identity is compared by byte range because web-tree-sitter re-creates Node wrappers per call (=== never holds). Pure AST, never source-text scanning.

decisions.question: PHP global function calls flood the graph with stdlib edges — filter or keep?
decisions.resolution: PHP_BUILTINS (exported set, ~200 stdlib globals: string/array/type/math/fs/control/preg families) are filtered from call relationships. Method calls (member/scoped/nullsafe) are NEVER filtered — they are user code. The differential oracle imports the analyzer's EXACT set (single source of truth, no hand-duplicated copy).

decisions.question: Where do `use App\Models\User;` imports land — references or imports?
decisions.resolution: imports array ONLY (module = FQN, items = [alias or leaf]). The references relationship kind is reserved for require/include expression file paths (emitInclude). The differential oracle mirrors this split exactly.

decisions.question: Interface inheritance (`interface A extends B, C`) uses the same base_clause node as class extends — how are they distinguished?
decisions.resolution: By container node type: inside interface_declaration, base_clause children are ALL extends targets (interfaces inherit multiple parents); inside class_declaration, base_clause has exactly ONE child = the superclass (extends), and class_interface_clause children are implements. The dead literal 'interface_base_clause' (older grammar) was removed — probe-verified against the pinned wasm 2026-08-30.

decisions.node_type: method_signature / method_declaration / function_definition / def / sub (override resolution)
decisions.question: AnalyzeContext.overrideCompanion is never populated by production callers — what must analyzers that gate ALL override emission on it do for externally-declared bases?
decisions.resolution: M37.10 ruling (family-wide): the companion is optional enrichment, never a hard gate. Contract: in-file base declaring the method -> verified override (0.95 php/ruby/python/js/perl, 1.0 java/swift Pass-1); companion present -> companion-index resolution (0.85-0.9); otherwise deterministic Pass-3 first-parent guess at 0.5 with reasonCode 'first-parent-guess' and evidence tier 'inferred' — below the patterns.ts 0.7 threshold, counted as heuristic (honest suspicion) by the F5 differential. Gating on the companion alone silently dropped every cross-file override (php, ruby, python, javascript, perl); the inverse overclaim (swift guess at 1.0/structural) is equally a defect. Gated by F9-PROBE-M3710-* probes, per-language external-override fixtures + confidence pins, and 6 regression mutants.

decisions.question: M37.13 (php dual-lens #606): the extractive walk only recursed into node types it matched, and the call/creation processors (function_call / member_call / scoped_call / object_creation) lived ONLY inside walkBody (method/function bodies). Statements at program scope in PHP scripts, config/bootstrap files, and WP/plugin hook files ($x = new App(); $app->boot(); register_shutdown_function(...)) were silently dropped — the analyzer emitted ZERO edges for them while the differential oracle (a generic walk) derived all of them. Why was the corpus differential green despite this?
decisions.resolution: phpunit is class-heavy: only 4/300 sampled files (1.3%) carry top-level call statements, so the 60-file F5 sample rarely hit the shape — a coverage blind spot exactly like haskell HSD12/CSD1. Fix (M37.13): the main walk now dispatches function_call/member_call/nullsafe/scoped_call/object_creation wherever reached OUTSIDE a body, plus a generic child-recursion fallback for every unmatched node (mirroring the oracle's generic walk). Member READS are deliberately NOT dispatched there: the oracle derives uses for member_access only inside method/function bodies (inBody), which never reach the extractive walk (walkBody owns bodies) — verified parity on closures/arrows (anonymous_function/arrow_function are not body contexts in the oracle either). Pinned by fixtures/php/procedural-enum (global-sourced instantiates/calls equals pins) + mutant php/drop-top-level-procedural.

decisions.question: M37.13: PHP 8.1 enums implement interfaces via the same class_interface_clause shape as classes ('enum Status implements Labeled'), but the enum_declaration branch never read the clause, and the oracle mirrored the blind spot — enum implements edges were dropped by BOTH sides (a shared hole no differential can see).
decisions.resolution: Fix (M37.13): analyzer reads class_interface_clause on enum_declaration and emits implements edges (metadata isEnumImplements, tier structural) + implementedInterfaces payload; the oracle mirrors the same clause read so truth and analyzer stay in sync. Corpus-zero in phpunit (1 enum, 0 clauses in 300 files) so fixture + mutant gate it: fixtures/php/procedural-enum pins implements Status->Labeled/Tagged; mutant php/drop-enum-implements dies.

decisions.question: M37.13: the analyzer's processFunctionCall returns EARLY for the WordPress hook registrars add_action/add_filter (framework detection only, never a calls edge — they register callbacks, they don't call user code). The differential oracle imported the analyzer's PHP_BUILTINS but NOT this hook exclusion, so it fabricated calls:add_action/add_filter truth on every procedural WP-style file.
decisions.resolution: Ruling (M37.13): WP hook registration is framework ceremony — excluded from call edges on BOTH sides (single exclusion mirrored in derivePhpEdges, never a hand-duplicated copy). Add_action/add_filter still trigger WordPress framework detection. Pinned by fixtures/php/procedural-enum forbidRelationships (calls->add_action/add_filter) + mutant php/emit-wp-hook-calls.

decisions.node_type: method_declaration inside anonymous_class at top level
decisions.question: M37.13: 'new class { public function handle() {...} }' at top level — once the generic fallback descends into anonymous_class, its method_declaration nodes reached the extractive walk with owner=undefined and fabricated ownerless method symbols (a class-body member always carries its owner via pushMembers, so ownerless methods can ONLY come from anonymous classes).
decisions.resolution: Fix (M37.13): ownerless method_declaration = anonymous-class method — never symbolized (the class has no nameable symbol; mirrors walkBody's treatment of anon classes nested inside named methods), but the body IS walked so calls/creations inside are preserved (global-sourced). Pinned by fixtures/php/procedural-enum forbidSymbols handle + mutant php/symbolize-anon-class-methods.

decisions.question: M37.13: PHP 8.1 'new in initializers' (parameter default values, attribute arguments, static-variable and global-constant initializers) — these live in method/function SIGNATURES which the extractive walk continues past (bodies only). The generic walk would find the object_creation; the analyzer currently does not descend signatures.
decisions.resolution: Ruling (M37.13): documented boundary. Census on phpunit (300 files): 0 signature/attribute-context `new` occurrences (168 attribute_list nodes, none carrying object_creation). Corpus-zero shape; recorded here so the boundary is explicit rather than accidental. If a corpus ever exercises it, descend formal_parameters/attribute_list after walkBody with the same dispatch (no member reads possible there — signatures hold constant expressions).

decisions.node_type: base_clause / class_interface_clause with same-leaf fully-qualified base (namespace collision)
decisions.question: M37.13: a class may inherit from a DIFFERENT class that shares its leaf name in another namespace — phpmyadmin Setup\FeaturesForm extends User\FeaturesForm, phpunit interface Exception extends \PHPUnit\Exception, class InvalidArgumentException extends \InvalidArgumentException (the SPL builtin). Everything was leaf-collapsed, so the subclass's own name matched the base leaf: fabricated extends Self edges (12 in phpunit, 11 in phpmyadmin), VERIFIED @0.95 self-overrides (16 phpmyadmin, 2 phpunit — the in-file/companion override check matched the class's OWN methods), and `new parent()` -> self. Why did the F5 differential stay green? Both the analyzer AND the oracle leaf-collapsed identically — extends truth fabricated on both sides colluded.
decisions.resolution: Fix (M37.13): heritage-target resolution (heritageTarget). A QUALIFIED base/interface whose leaf equals the declaring class's name keeps its qualification (leading backslash stripped): extends FeaturesForm -> Forms\User\FeaturesForm, and override resolution then runs against the external same-leaf base (M37.10 first-parent guess @0.5/inferred — never verified, never self). A qualified base that qualification CANNOT disambiguate — global single-segment like \InvalidArgumentException — is unresolvable in the leaf graph: NO extends edge and no baseByClass entry (self-loop is always fabrication; family 'wrong edge worse than no edge' precedent, same as unresolvable new parent()). Analyzer metadata.baseClass/extends/implements/enum-implements and oracle derivePhpEdges + deriveTreeEdges heritage all mirror the same helper. Corpus result: self-extends 12->0 (phpunit), 11->0 (phpmyadmin); self-overrides 16->0 / 2->0; differential parity held at 100%/0/0 on both corpora.

decisions.question: M37.13 follow-up wave-2 (#606 master-review): PHP 8 nullsafe member READS `$this->svc?->name` parse as nullsafe_member_access_expression with the SAME "name" field as member_access_expression (`$this->svc->name`), but the walkBody member-read branch only matched member_access_expression, so every nullsafe read silently dropped the trailing member uses edge. 20 occurrences across phpunit+phpmyadmin+slim (4,231 files). Differential-invisible: the oracle's derivePhpEdges member branch shared the same shallow type gate, so F5 parity held at 0 missing / 0 unexplained while both sides dropped the read.
decisions.resolution: Fix (wave-2 probe-verified 2026-09-07): walkBody member-read branch now matches member_access_expression OR nullsafe_member_access_expression; the read/write + call-receiver byte-range gate is unchanged, so nullsafe WRITES (`$this->feature?->name = $v`) and RMW (`$this->feature?->name .= '!'`) stay gated exactly like the plain form (LHS name never a read). The receiver member (`$this->svc` / `$this->feature`) emits its own uses in both forms (csharp/java/ruby family precedent: the container is fetched to dereference). Oracle mirror identical. Parity probe: read/chain/plain emit [name, svc]/[deep, inner, svc]; write/augwrite emit only [svc]. Pinned by fixtures/php/nullsafe-member-reads (expect describe->name / describe->nested / describe->feature uses; forbid rewrite->name / bump->name) + mutants php/drop-nullsafe-member-read-uses and php/emit-nullsafe-write-as-uses both CAUGHT (299/299).

decisions.question: OO family closure #613 family sweep: php `$x instanceof Foo` emits NO edge on either side while java (instanceof_expression) and python (isinstance/issubclass) emit references:instanceof_check from their declared-type reference graphs. Corpus: ~950 instanceof sites in the two php corpora (phpunit 799, phpmyadmin 153) are silent. Is php dropping a relationship the family convention requires?
decisions.resolution: RULED consistent-as-designed: php has no declared-type reference graph — its references channel is include-only (PHPD3); type hints (named_type in parameter/return positions) are SYMBOL payload, never edges — matching csharp (is/as silent), swift (as?/is silent) and objc (isKindOfClass: silent). python/java materialize those edges because their analyzers carry a declared-type reference extraction pass php does not have. Adding instanceof references to php alone would create a family asymmetry in the other direction and require re-pinning both php F5 lanes. Recorded as a measured scope decision, not a hidden skip (both sides silent = differential-consistent 100/0/0).

decisions.question: First review: `$this->dep->run()` and `$a->b->c()` skipped the receiver read (isCallReceiver gate) while nullsafe chains already emitted their links — plain chains inconsistently silent on both sides.
decisions.resolution: Receivers ARE reads (must evaluate to dispatch); only the call's own name is the target. Gate dropped on both sides. Gated by fixture php/member-value-reads receiver pins + mutant php/drop-receiver-read-uses.

decisions.question: First review: scoped CALLS (`C::create()`) always covered, but static property reads (`C::$total`, `self::$x`, `parent::$x`, `static::$x`) invisible on both sides.
decisions.resolution: Reads emit uses with the member write gate; scopes (types/relative_scope) never read. Gated by fixture + mutants php/drop-static-read-uses, php/emit-static-write-as-uses.

decisions.question: First review: constant fetches (`Suit::Hearts`, `parent::VERSION`) invisible on both sides (dart emits enum members the same way). No name field exists — positional [scope, name]; `::class` is a keyword.
decisions.resolution: Last name child reads; ::class skipped. A first-name lookup would read the scope (caught by probe, fixed pre-lane). Gated by fixture + mutants php/drop-const-fetch-uses, php/const-fetch-scope-leak.

decisions.question: First review: `$this->handler(...)`, `strlen(...)`, `Widget::make(...)` emitted calls — but sole-`...` never invokes (first-class callable tear-off). Mixed `($x, ...)` genuinely invokes (error-recovering in the pinned grammar).
decisions.resolution: Sole-placeholder calls emit uses (builtins still filtered); mixed forms stay calls. Gated by fixture + mutant php/tearoff-as-call.

decisions.question: First review: `"hello $name"`, `"sum {$n}"`, `"{$o->p}"` — simple interpolations invisible on both sides (only member_access inside fired). Interpolation is pervasive in PHP (WordPress).
decisions.resolution: Blanket reads (dart DT-F parity): variable_name under encapsed/dynamic strings + name-under-dynamic; $this skipped. Gated by fixture + mutant php/drop-interp-read-uses.

decisions.question: First review: `$a['k']` bases invisible on both sides (dart DT-F parity; write-position bases read the address per OC-E).
decisions.resolution: First-named-child base reads, no inventory; indexes are bare values (review 2). Gated by fixture + mutant php/drop-subscript-read-uses.

decisions.question: First review: `use ($factor)` captures copy outer values — invisible on both sides. Arrow-fn implicit captures need inventory.
decisions.resolution: Clause names read structurally; implicit captures defer to review 2 (documented split). Gated by fixture + mutant php/drop-capture-read-uses.

decisions.question: First review: every trait use was analyzer-only — the oracle gated use_declaration on inBody, which is never true at class level. Lanes missed it by sampling luck (no trait-use file drawn in 200).
decisions.resolution: Oracle gate dropped (analyzer always emitted). Companion mutant guards the analyzer side; lanes guard the oracle side.

decisions.question: First review: verified in-file overrides (0.95) were analyzer-only — the oracle derived no overrides at all, an unexplained edge waiting for a sample (synthetic A/B pair reproduces).
decisions.resolution: Oracle prescan (class -> resolved base + declared methods) emits verified pairs; external guesses stay silent (0.5, below lane filter).

decisions.question: First review: `$this->run($x, ...)` error-recovers (ERROR node) — call or tear-off? And `new class extends Base` heritage?
decisions.resolution: Mixed forms genuinely invoke AND error-recover with the callee as member access — both sides derive uses (documented boundary imprecision, never calls). Anonymous classes have no nameable identity: heritage/construction silent on both sides.

decisions.question: First review: identical call sites emit duplicate rows (`calls[m->run]` x2) — DARTD7-style dedup or retain?
decisions.resolution: RETAINED at emit: expectRelationshipCount pins multiplicity (instantiates == 2) and the differential is presence-based. The store dedups by (source, target, type) relId (verified live: zero duplicate groups) — hover counts distinct edges, not sites. Analyzer multiplicity and store dedup coexist by design; DARTD7 does not transfer.

decisions.question: First review: `$depth`/`$total` RHS, `$a + $b`, `[$this, 'm']` callables, `instanceof`, `clone $x`, match subjects — all silent on both sides.
decisions.resolution: Bare value reads need scope inventory: deferred to review 2 with the member-read foundation landed here (same split as dart DT-F). Operators are arithmetic dispatch; string-literal callables unresolvable by design; instanceof already ruled (PHPD19).

decisions.question: Second review (implements deferred PHP-R3): bare `$var` occurrences outside member/call/subscript/use/interpolation positions were silent on both sides — when is a bare variable a READ?
decisions.resolution: Reads resolve through a scope inventory: innermost frame chain (params/locals/use/catch/foreach/list/static/global decls; closures fresh, arrows chained, named functions fresh), then file-scope function names, then superglobals — anything else is silent (no hallucinated globals). `$this` never reads. Declaration/write/label positions never read (isPhpBindSite: params incl. promoted, static/global decls, catch vars, assignment LHS incl. destructuring, foreach value/key incl. the BARE `as $item` form, use-clause vars are READS not binds). Subscript bases and index positions belong to the PHP-B rule; use-clause/interpolation interiors belong to PHP-C/PHP-F. Analyzer emits isLocalRead/isGlobalRead; oracle mirrors the identical frame logic. Gated by fixture php/bare-value-reads + 3 loss mutants + battery/lanes parity.

decisions.question: Second review: bare `NAME` constants (`LIMIT`, `ROOT_PATH`, `RUN_NAME`) were silent — when is a bare name a const READ?
decisions.resolution: Only when the name sits in the file const inventory (top-level const, class consts are members not bare values, define() names incl. same-file defines via the file prescan, use-const imports). Magic constants (__DIR__ etc.) never read. Member/callee/const-fetch/heritage positions belong to other rules; named-argument labels, namespace/use bindings, type positions (param/return/catch/instanceof/new), and declaration first-names (const_element, enum_case — positional, only the first name declares) never read. Class-level reads attribute to the owner class (trait-use PHP-O1 precedent), not global. Analyzer emits isConstRead; oracle mirrors. Gated by fixture php/bare-value-reads + drop-bare-const-reads mutant.

decisions.question: Second review: `foreach ($xs as $item)` bound nothing — the value variable sits DIRECTLY under foreach_statement (no `pair` wrapper, unlike `as $k => $v`), so both the analyzer and its mirror missed the bind and the body read. Battery agreed (shared mirror miss).
decisions.resolution: A variable_name directly under foreach_statement that is not the first named child (the collection, which reads) is a bind site — analyzer isPhpBindSite + oracle phpIsBindSite fixed as a mirrored pair. By-reference values (`as &$v`) bind the same way. Found only because the fixture is independent of the mirror. Gated by fixture php/bare-value-reads item pin + battery probe foreach_bare.

decisions.node_type: call receivers (base variables) + class-level read attribution
decisions.question: Second review: `$gw->authorize()` emitted no read for `$gw` (wave-1 `receivers excluded` held for the single-link base while PHP-A chains already read links — incoherent), and class-level const reads (property/const/enum/attribute/default initializers) sourced global instead of the class.
decisions.resolution: Receiver BASE variables read as ordinary bare values (the object value loads to dispatch); the exclusion now holds only on the MEMBER side (no uses-read of the method name — payload-and-complexity authorize/dispatch forbids). Class-level reads attribute to the owner (inFunction || owner || global). The wave-1 blanket `uses->gateway` forbid encoded the old contract and is replaced by member-side forbids + variable-side expects; php/emit-write-as-uses is retargeted to file-scope writes (its old fabrication became legitimate output). Gated by payload-and-complexity expects/forbids + php/emit-receiver-member-read mutant + owner-attribution pins in bare-value-reads (Reader->LIMIT/RUN_NAME/FALLBACK, Level->RUN_NAME).

decisions.node_type: php_tag, text_interpolation, text, encapsed_string, heredoc, nowdoc
decisions.question: The php wave (#268 family) declared this a gap: 'HTML/text interpolation segments outside <?php blocks are not symbols; string interpolation internals are opaque'. Is that a gap or a ruling?
decisions.resolution: RULED, not a gap. A `use`d requirement of this lane is a SYMBOL CONTRACT over PHP declarations, and the text outside `<?php ... ?>` is not PHP: it is the template that PHP is embedded in, and its `$var` slots belong to whatever templating engine wrote them (Twig, Blade, Smarty), not to PHP's grammar. Emitting symbols for interpolated HTML would invent PHP declarations that do not exist. The string-interpolation half of the old gap text is separately adjudicated and IS handled: "hello $name" (simple), "{$o->p}" (object/member), and "{$n['k']}" style forms are read for VALUE flow by the in-PHP rules, pinned by php/bare-value-reads and php/header-reads. The old wording conflated two different things — a correct boundary on out-of-PHP text, and an unfinished job on in-PHP interpolation that was in fact finished. Recording it as a `gap` therefore reported finished work as outstanding forever.

decisions.question: The php wave (#268 family) declared this a gap: 'ini directives and shell hash-bang lines are not parsed as symbols or decision points'. Is that a gap or a ruling?
decisions.resolution: RULED, not a gap. `ini_section`/`ini_entry` are .ini FILES parsed by PHP's own INI machinery, not by this analyzer — no PHP declaration exists in them to miss, and the same applies to a `#!` hash-bang line, which is the OS's interpreter directive. The `preprocessor`/`shell_comment` nodes that appear in a .php file are likewise not PHP declarations. Declaring symbols for any of these would put non-PHP constructs into a PHP symbol graph. The grammar emits these node types for these files and the analyzer correctly declares nothing for them, which is a boundary, not unfinished work.
